observations.statement: The assigned core identifies the artifact as schema pm.wiring_matrix.v0.
Seven complete core entries map the Cancel, Open In Browser, Pin, Rerun, Rerun Failed, Show, and Switch Subview context-action UI locations to distinct command IDs and handler locations.

All seven complete entries declare an empty expected_event_types array, and their effect descriptions say there is no declared persisted event while requiring a no-persist command receipt or route/open disposition.
Each complete entry names a per-command availability selector and a corresponding disabled-reason projection.

The cancel entry requires dispatch evidence to preserve command_id, origin, correlation_id, handler target, result, and the receipt or event effect, and it supplies dispatcher, state-projection, effect, accessibility, and no-unexpected-event test requirements.

The cancel accessibility contract explicitly covers stable role/name/description, keyboard reachability and activation, deterministic focus handling after dispatch or error, and assistive-technology announcement of the disabled reason.

Production certification for cancel explicitly requires render/control evidence, a dispatcher fixture, typed payload/result assertion, projected-state and disabled-reason proof, receipt/event assertion, accessibility checking, and regression-test evidence.

candidate_findings.title: Typed command contracts are required but not defined
candidate_findings.statement: All seven complete entries require typed args/result or typed payload/result contracts, but the assigned core provides no payload fields, field types, requiredness rules, validation constraints, result variants, or error variants for any of the commands.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders cannot derive a single interoperable dispatcher ABI or a deterministic typed-contract certification oracle from this window, so independently implemented handlers can disagree while claiming the same wiring.

candidate_findings.title: Command-specific capability behavior is left to builders
candidate_findings.statement: Beyond UI names, command IDs, handler locations, and generic no-persist receipt wording, the assigned core does not define the target identity, command-specific preconditions, successful outcome, or command-specific failure behavior for Cancel, Open In Browser, Pin, Rerun, Rerun Failed, Show, or Switch Subview.
candidate_findings.impact: The observable meaning of these capabilities can diverge across implementations, especially for cancel, pin, and rerun actions whose targets and allowed states are consequential.

candidate_findings.title: Receipt versus route/open disposition is ambiguous
candidate_findings.statement: The effect contract labels the effect_kind as receipt and provides a dispatch_receipt reference, but its description permits either a no-persist command receipt or a route/open disposition; the selection rule and the route/open disposition schema are not specified.
candidate_findings.impact: Dispatch evidence and tests can encode incompatible effect records, weakening correlation, failure diagnosis, and production-certification comparability.

candidate_findings.title: Availability and disabled-reason state semantics are underspecified
candidate_findings.statement: The entries name availability and disabled-reason paths and require them before dispatch, but the core does not define their value types, allowed states, derivation rules, refresh timing, or consistency relationship.
candidate_findings.impact: Controls can disagree about when a command is enabled, expose stale disabled copy, or race dispatch against changing state while still reading the prescribed paths.

candidate_findings.title: Dispatch failure and repeated-invocation lifecycle are unspecified
candidate_findings.statement: Dispatch evidence must include a result and focus must return deterministically after dispatch or error, but the core defines no timeout, cancellation-race, retry, idempotency, concurrency, partial-failure, or error-to-result semantics.
candidate_findings.impact: Repeated or concurrent invocations can produce inconsistent handler effects, receipts, and focus outcomes, with no window-local oracle for which behavior is conforming.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: The core does not leave UI-to-command-to-handler routing implicit for the seven complete entries; each has a concrete UI location, command ID, and handler location.
The core supplies explicit availability and disabled-reason projection paths for every complete entry.
For cancel, the no-persist expectation has an explicit receipt-or-disposition assertion and prohibits unexpected persisted domain events.
For cancel, acceptance evidence is not left as a generic testing instruction; named requirements cover dispatcher routing, state projection, effect assertion, and accessibility regression.
The accessibility contract explicitly covers role semantics, keyboard operation, focus management, and disabled-state announcement.
The dispatch evidence requirement explicitly enumerates command identity, origin, correlation, handler target, result, and effect information that must be preserved.

unknowns.statement: Whether concrete typed payload and result definitions exist outside the assigned window cannot be determined from the authorized evidence.
The authority that approves production certification and the consumers, persistence location, retention period, and query contract for dispatch receipts are not identified in the assigned core.
The generation, type, uniqueness, and propagation rules for origin and correlation_id cannot be determined from the dispatch-evidence requirement.
It cannot be determined whether availability selectors are synchronous snapshots or subscribed projections, or when disabled reasons must update relative to state transitions.

The context range begins the catalog.actions_unpin entry but ends before its selector, effect, accessibility, and test sections, so no complete assessment of unpin can be made and it is not used for a core finding.
It is not explicit whether expected_event_types being empty prohibits every emitted event or only persisted domain events; the event test only forbids unexpected persisted domain events.
